queries.search_text: site:digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu AI Act timeline 2026 obligations high-risk systems official
queries.source_title: AI Act | Shaping Europe’s digital future
queries.proposition: The European Commission describes distinct provider and deployer duties, transparency rules effective from August 2026, GPAI duties effective from August 2025, high-risk obligations staged for December 2027 or August 2028, and enforcement shared between the AI Office and national authorities.
queries.status: SUPPORTED for rule timing and role separation; willingness to pay is UNKNOWN
queries.contradiction: The staged dates and simplified obligations for smaller firms weaken any claim that every AI user needs the same immediate compliance package; most AI systems are described as minimal or no risk.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Offer a fixed-price classification-and-evidence sprint to ten Polish HR, health, finance, and vertical-software operators and require a paid deposit from at least two before building software.

queries.search_text: site:ure.gov.pl 2026 Poland dynamic electricity tariffs smart meters prosumers official
queries.source_title: Już ponad 4,8 tys. gospodarstw domowych korzysta z umów z cenami dynamicznymi
queries.proposition: Poland’s regulator reports that dynamic-price contracts require remotely read meters, settle against market movements at intervals of at least 15 minutes, reached 4,836 households and 27,000 small or microbusiness customers by end-2025, and produced materially different average prices depending largely on consumption profile.
queries.status: SUPPORTED for market mechanics and adoption; commercial demand for optimization services is UNKNOWN
queries.contradiction: Household penetration remained below 0.03 percent, only four of ten sellers achieved average household prices below the protected 500 PLN/MWh level, and switching exposed households to loss of the 2025 protection mechanism.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Analyze exported interval data and bills for twenty eligible small businesses, then sell a no-hardware savings verification pilot whose fee is contingent on measured improvement.

concepts.title: AI Role-and-Date Evidence Vault
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A lightweight evidence vault can tell mid-market companies which AI systems they provide or deploy, which deadlines actually apply, and which missing artifacts need an owner.
concepts.customer: Polish employers and vertical-software firms using AI in hiring, credit, education, or other potentially high-risk workflows
concepts.loss_event: A system is misclassified or reaches an enforcement date without traceable documentation, creating remediation delay, deal friction, or regulatory exposure.
concepts.payer: General counsel, compliance lead, or software product owner
concepts.beneficiary: Compliance, procurement, product, and internal audit teams
concepts.authority_holder: The company officer accountable for placing or using the system, with regulators retaining enforcement authority
concepts.distributor: Boutique law firms, ISO advisers, and cyber-risk brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: The provider or deployer remains legally responsible; the service bears only contracted professional-liability risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed-fee inventory and role-classification workshop producing an evidence-gap register
concepts.acquisition_route: Partner referrals from Polish privacy, employment, and technology-law advisers
concepts.compounding_asset: An anonymized library of system patterns, role decisions, evidence requests, and remediation durations
hypotheses: Target firms have enough deployed AI to make manual inventories painful.
Legal advisers will refer execution work without treating the product as unauthorized legal advice.
A narrow paid workshop converts into recurring evidence maintenance.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not present automated classification as definitive legal advice or shift statutory responsibility away from the provider or deployer.

concepts.title: Synthetic-Media Disclosure Gateway
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: An API and approval queue can insert machine-readable provenance and visible AI disclosures into agency and publisher export workflows before content is released.
concepts.customer: Polish creative agencies, branded-content studios, and online publishers producing AI-assisted media
concepts.loss_event: Synthetic content ships without required identification or visible labelling, forcing takedown, rework, or client escalation.
concepts.payer: Agency operations director or publisher compliance owner
concepts.beneficiary: Editors, clients, audiences, and compliance teams
concepts.authority_holder: The content publisher or deployer approving public release
concepts.distributor: Digital asset-management vendors and agency production consultants
concepts.risk_bearer: The publisher retains compliance risk; the gateway bears service-availability and processing-error risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid integration for one content pipeline and one disclosure policy
concepts.acquisition_route: Direct outreach to operations leaders through agency software integrators
concepts.compounding_asset: A format-by-platform rules engine and corpus of disclosure exceptions and failed exports
hypotheses: Publishers have repeatable export points where disclosure controls can be inserted.
Existing content tools do not reliably preserve required provenance across transformations.
Buyers will pay to reduce manual pre-publication review.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not falsely certify content origin or imply that adding a label cures prohibited or rights-infringing content.

concepts.title: GPAI Downstream Documentation Relay
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A structured relay can convert model-provider documentation into versioned, customer-ready capability, limitation, copyright, and change records for small vertical AI vendors.
concepts.customer: European vertical SaaS vendors building on third-party general-purpose AI models
concepts.loss_event: A model or policy change leaves downstream customers without current information needed for procurement, risk review, or their own compliance work.
concepts.payer: Chief technology officer or product compliance lead
concepts.beneficiary: Enterprise customers, product teams, and risk reviewers
concepts.authority_holder: The SaaS provider that places its AI system on the market
concepts.distributor: Cloud consultancies, model-platform resellers, and AI assurance advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: The SaaS provider retains product obligations; the relay bears contractual risk for missed or malformed updates.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed-fee conversion of one model stack into a customer-facing documentation pack
concepts.acquisition_route: Co-selling through implementation partners serving regulated vertical SaaS firms
concepts.compounding_asset: A normalized change graph linking model versions, vendor notices, system uses, and downstream artifacts
hypotheses: Vertical vendors repeatedly repackage overlapping model documentation for customers.
Model changes create a recurring update burden large enough to support subscription pricing.
Providers permit lawful ingestion and transformation of their documentation.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not invent missing upstream evidence or represent a transformed pack as an official conformity assessment.

concepts.title: Role-Specific AI Literacy Ledger
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A short scenario-based training service can give employers auditable evidence that staff received AI instruction matched to the systems and decisions they actually control.
concepts.customer: Employers whose staff procure, configure, supervise, or rely on AI systems
concepts.loss_event: Staff misuse an AI system or the employer cannot show who was trained on which risks and controls.
concepts.payer: HR director, compliance officer, or information-security lead
concepts.beneficiary: Employees, affected customers, and the employer’s control functions
concepts.authority_holder: Employer management sets required training and system access
concepts.distributor: Occupational training firms, HR software implementers, and insurers
concepts.risk_bearer: The employer retains responsibility for competence and supervision; the service bears content-quality risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: Learning and development or compliance manager
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid cohort covering one job family and issuing evidence records after scenario checks
concepts.acquisition_route: White-label distribution through existing mandatory-training providers
concepts.compounding_asset: A library of role-specific failure scenarios and aggregated misconception data
hypotheses: Generic AI courses do not satisfy buyers seeking role-specific evidence.
Training partners want a white-label module instead of building AI scenarios internally.
Annual refreshes and workforce changes create repeat revenue.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not claim that course completion alone establishes legal compliance or operational competence.

concepts.title: AI Incident Handoff Network
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A neutral incident intake and handoff service can connect deployers, providers, and advisers around traceable malfunction reports without requiring a full governance suite.
concepts.customer: Providers and deployers of AI used in employment, essential services, health, and regulated products
concepts.loss_event: A serious malfunction is discovered but evidence, ownership, and notification decisions fragment across customer, vendor, and counsel.
concepts.payer: Risk, quality, or product operations lead
concepts.beneficiary: Affected users, providers, deployers, insurers, and regulators
concepts.authority_holder: The provider or deployer’s designated incident decision-maker
concepts.distributor: Professional indemnity brokers, quality-management consultants, and managed service providers
concepts.risk_bearer: Each regulated actor retains reporting duties; the network bears secure-routing and evidentiary-integrity risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid tabletop exercise followed by activation of a shared incident channel
concepts.acquisition_route: Broker-led sale bundled with cyber or professional-liability renewal
concepts.compounding_asset: An anonymized taxonomy of incident signatures, routing paths, missing evidence, and resolution times
hypotheses: Cross-company handoffs are a larger failure point than initial incident detection.
Insurers or advisers can aggregate enough customers to lower acquisition cost.
Buyers will pay before reporting rules fully apply in their category.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not suppress reportable incidents, predetermine legal reportability, or expose personal and confidential incident data beyond authorized parties.

concepts.title: Small-Business Load-Shift Autopilot
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A meter-data optimizer can schedule flexible refrigeration, heating, charging, and production loads against dynamic energy and distribution prices while respecting operating constraints.
concepts.customer: Polish bakeries, cold stores, workshops, farms, and small facilities with remotely read meters and flexible electrical loads
concepts.loss_event: The business consumes heavily in costly intervals or shifts load in ways that disrupt production and erase expected tariff savings.
concepts.beneficiary: The operating business and, when aligned, the electricity system
concepts.authority_holder: Facility owner approves control limits and tariff choice
concepts.distributor: Regional electricians, renewable installers, and energy sellers
concepts.risk_bearer: The customer bears tariff exposure; the service bears contracted control-error risk within agreed limits.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid interval-data audit identifying a load-shift plan before any device control
concepts.acquisition_route: Installer referrals using prior customer relationships in Wielkopolska
concepts.compounding_asset: A device-and-business-type library of flexibility envelopes and verified savings
hypotheses: A meaningful subset of small businesses has controllable load and compatible meters.
Measured savings exceed integration and behavior-change costs.
Owners accept automation when hard operating limits and manual override are present.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not control safety-critical equipment without explicit limits, fail-safe behavior, and qualified installation.

concepts.title: Tariff-Aware Retrofit Proof
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A pre-sale simulator can show installers and customers whether batteries, heat pumps, or EV charging improve bills under the customer’s actual interval profile rather than generic savings claims.
concepts.customer: Renewable and electrical installers selling storage, heat pumps, or charging to homes and microbusinesses
concepts.loss_event: An incorrectly sized retrofit disappoints the buyer because its economics ignore load timing, tariff exposure, or operating behavior.
concepts.payer: Installer sales director or project customer
concepts.beneficiary: Installer, equipment buyer, and finance provider
concepts.authority_holder: Property or business owner authorizes the capital purchase
concepts.risk_bearer: The buyer bears investment performance unless the installer offers a guarantee; the simulator bears calculation-quality risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid branded feasibility report attached to one live equipment quote
concepts.acquisition_route: Embed the report in installer sales proposals and finance applications
concepts.compounding_asset: A dataset linking interval profiles, equipment designs, quoted assumptions, and post-installation outcomes
concepts.mechanism_class: decision model embedded in channel sales
hypotheses: Installers lose deals or margin because customers distrust generic payback estimates.
Customers can authorize access to sufficient meter and bill data.
Post-installation measurement can improve future sizing without privacy abuse.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not promise savings without stated scenarios, uncertainty, and verification boundaries.

concepts.title: Dynamic Tariff Tender Desk
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: An independent tender desk can compare dynamic offers on a microbusiness’s own load profile and manage switching, renewal, and exception review.
concepts.customer: Polish microbusinesses eligible for dynamic-price electricity offers
concepts.loss_event: A buyer selects an offer using headline prices, then pays more because fees and its consumption profile were poorly matched.
concepts.authority_holder: Authorized signatory for the electricity contract
concepts.distributor: Accountancy offices, business associations, and energy-efficiency advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: The customer retains wholesale-price exposure; the desk bears comparison and process-error risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed-fee offer comparison using twelve months of interval data and all-in contract terms
concepts.acquisition_route: White-label service through accountants serving energy-intensive microbusinesses
concepts.compounding_asset: A normalized database of offer terms, realized profile costs, switching friction, and seller performance
hypotheses: Microbusiness owners lack time or tools to compare offers on interval data.
Accountants can distribute a clearly bounded procurement service.
Sellers permit independent comparison and customers will pay without hidden commissions.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must disclose commissions and conflicts and must not imply that dynamic pricing is always cheaper.

concepts.title: Flexible-Load Savings Warranty
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A data-led warranty can reimburse part of the shortfall when an approved load-shifting plan fails to reach a conservative, independently measured savings threshold.
concepts.customer: Installers and energy-service firms selling controls to small commercial sites
concepts.loss_event: The customer rejects or disputes a project because modeled savings do not materialize after tariff and behavior changes.
concepts.payer: Installer or energy-service company embedding the warranty in its proposal
concepts.authority_holder: Warranty underwriter sets eligibility, measurement, and payout terms
concepts.distributor: Renewable installers and equipment finance brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: A licensed insurer or authorized warranty provider bears defined performance shortfall; the analytics operator bears model and data-processing risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid eligibility analysis and warranty quote for one proposed installation
concepts.acquisition_route: Point-of-sale attachment to storage and control-system proposals
concepts.compounding_asset: A loss curve by load profile, tariff, device, installer, and control policy
hypotheses: Performance uncertainty is a material blocker in equipment sales.
Claims can be measured from authorized meter data with limited moral hazard.
A regulated risk carrier will underwrite a narrowly defined product at viable terms.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not self-underwrite regulated insurance without authorization or manipulate the savings baseline to avoid valid payouts.

concepts.title: Dynamic-Customer Retention Signals
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A privacy-preserving analytics feed can warn electricity sellers when a dynamic-price customer’s profile is producing poor outcomes and trigger an appropriate tariff or coaching review.
concepts.customer: Polish electricity retailers offering dynamic contracts to households and microbusinesses
concepts.loss_event: Customers experience avoidable bill shock, complain, churn, or damage the seller’s reputation because the offer does not fit their load profile.
concepts.payer: Retail energy product or retention director
concepts.beneficiary: Customers, customer-service teams, and the retailer
concepts.authority_holder: The retailer controls outreach and offers; the customer controls any contract change.
concepts.distributor: Billing-platform vendors and smart-meter data integrators
concepts.risk_bearer: The retailer bears commercial and conduct risk; the analytics service bears signal-quality and data-security risk.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid retrospective churn-and-bill-shock analysis on a pseudonymized customer cohort
concepts.acquisition_route: Integration partnership with billing and customer-information-system vendors
concepts.compounding_asset: A cross-cohort library of profile-risk signals, intervention outcomes, and tariff-fit patterns
hypotheses: Retailers have sufficient consented interval and outcome data for analysis.
Poor tariff fit predicts complaints or churn early enough to intervene.
Retailers will fund retention despite the segment’s currently limited household scale.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not use interval data without a valid lawful basis, discriminate against vulnerable customers, or auto-switch contracts without customer authorization.
